554/2018, registered at Police Station Bhajanpura, Delhi for offences punishable under Sections 498A/406/34 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 (IPC) and all consequential proceedings emanating therefrom.
4. Issue notice.

sentences.text: After the round of multiple litigations between the parties, the parties entered into an MOU dated 21.10.2019 wherein they have arrived at full and final settlement of all their disputes/complaints and court cases, including her Stridhan, alimony/maintenance past present and future and all other claims arising out of and in connection with their marriage, and pursuant to which the parties have already taken divorce by Mutual Consent in 2019 itself.
7. Petitioner No.2 Sh. Vinod Giri and Petitioner No.4 Sh. Hemant Giri are stated to be expired.
8. The Petitioner No. 1 & 3 are present before this Court today, and have been identified by his counsel and the concerned Investigating Officer.
9. The Complainant/ Respondent No. 2 states that she has no objection if the FIR is quashed.
She has also given her No Objection and filed her Affidavit.
10. Learned prosecutor also submits that she has also no objection if the FIR is quashed.

11. In view of the above fact that the parties have amicably resolved their differences of their own free will, and without any coercion, no useful purpose will be served by continuing the proceedings

,
rather the same would create further acrimony between them.
It would thus, be in interest of justice to quash the abovementioned FIR and the proceedings pursuant thereto.
12. There is no legal impediment in quashing the FIR in question.
